eyebrow: Microsoft Azure Administration, Compute & Storage · Chapter 8
subtitle: Lesson 29 · Capstone: Deploying and Administering an Azure Environment

code:
az group create --name briarcliff-rg --location eastus \
  --tags environment=production costcenter=it-ops

az network vnet create --resource-group briarcliff-rg \
  --name briarcliff-vnet --address-prefix 10.20.0.0/16 \
  --subnet-name web-subnet --subnet-prefix 10.20.1.0/24

az network vnet subnet create --resource-group briarcliff-rg \
  --vnet-name briarcliff-vnet --name app-subnet \
  --address-prefix 10.20.2.0/24
caption: Tagged resource group first, then one VNet split into a web subnet and an app subnet.

code:
az vm create --resource-group briarcliff-rg --name web-vm1 \
  --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s \
  --vnet-name briarcliff-vnet --subnet web-subnet \
  --public-ip-address web-vm1-pip \
  --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys
caption: A real public IP — customers need to reach this one directly.

code:
az vm create --resource-group briarcliff-rg --name app-vm1 \
  --image Ubuntu2204 --size Standard_B2s \
  --vnet-name briarcliff-vnet --subnet app-subnet \
  --public-ip-address "" \
  --admin-username azureuser --generate-ssh-keys

az storage account create --resource-group briarcliff-rg \
  --name briarcliffdata001 --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2
caption: No public IP on the app VM — it should only ever hear from the web tier.

subtitle: Locking down the environment you just built, and watching it.
